By the symmetry of ![bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0200.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math>, ![bold-italic h Subscript j Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic upper A bold-italic h Subscript i Baseline equals bold-italic h Subscript i Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic upper A bold-italic h Subscript j](images/c01-i0201.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8868;</mo></mrow></msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8868;</mo></mrow></msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></math>, hence ![left-parenthesis lamda Subscript i Baseline minus lamda Subscript j Baseline right-parenthesis bold-italic h Subscript j Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic h Subscript i Baseline equals 0](images/c01-i0202.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8868;</mo></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. As ![lamda Subscript i Baseline not-equals lamda Subscript j](images/c01-i0203.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#8800;</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></math>, we must have ![bold-italic h Subscript j Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic h Subscript i Baseline equals 0](images/c01-i0204.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8868;</mo></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
7.  If ![bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0205.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math> is a ![p times p](images/c01-i0206.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></math> real symmetric matrix, then it has ![p](images/c01-i0207.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> orthogonal eigenvectors. Let ![bold-italic upper H](images/c01-i0208.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi></mrow></math> be a ![p times p](images/c01-i0209.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></math> matrix whose columns are normalized eigenvectors ![bold-italic h 1 comma ellipsis comma bold-italic h Subscript p Baseline](images/c01-i0210.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> of ![bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0211.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math>, i.e., ![bold-italic upper H equals left-parenthesis bold-italic h 1 comma ellipsis comma bold-italic h Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0212.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, then ![bold-italic upper H](images/c01-i0213.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi></mrow></math> is orthogonal, and
    
    ![bold-italic upper H Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic upper A bold-italic upper H equals bold-italic upper D equals diag left-parenthesis lamda 1 comma ellipsis comma lamda Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis left-parenthesis italic Diagonalization of bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis comma](images/c01-math-0023.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext>diag</mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="1em"/><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext mathvariant="italic">Diagonalization</mtext><mspace width="0.15em"/><mtext>of </mtext><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo></math> 
    
    or equivalently,
    
    ![bold-italic upper A equals bold-italic upper H bold-italic upper D bold-italic upper H Superscript down-tack Baseline left-parenthesis italic Spectral decomposition of bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis period](images/c01-math-0024.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext mathvariant="italic">Spectral decomposition</mtext><mspace width="0.15em"/><mtext>of </mtext><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>.</mo></math> 
    
    To see this, one can simply write ![bold-italic upper A bold-italic upper H equals left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A bold-italic h 1 comma ellipsis comma bold-italic upper A bold-italic h Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis equals left-parenthesis lamda 1 bold-italic h 1 comma ellipsis comma lamda Subscript p Baseline bold-italic h Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis equals bold-italic upper H bold-italic upper D](images/c01-i0214.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi></math>, therefore ![bold-italic upper H Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic upper A bold-italic upper H equals bold-italic upper D](images/c01-i0215.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi></math>.
    
8.  The trace of a matrix ![bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0216.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math> is the sum of all its eigenvalues and the determinant of ![bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0217.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math> is the product of all its eigenvalues, i.e., ![trace left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis equals sigma-summation Underscript i equals 1 Overscript p Endscripts lamda Subscript i Baseline](images/c01-i0218.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mtext>tr</mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8721;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math> and ![StartAbsoluteValue bold-italic upper A EndAbsoluteValue equals product Underscript i equals 1 Overscript p Endscripts lamda Subscript i](images/c01-i0219.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8719;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>, respectively.

**(VI) Symmetric square root of a positive semi-definite matrix**

Let ![bold-italic upper A succeeds-or-equal-to bold 0](images/c01-i0220.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>&#8829;</mo><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></math> be a ![p times p](images/c01-i0221.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></math> real symmetric matrix with non-negative eigenvalues ![lamda 1 comma ellipsis comma lamda Subscript p Baseline](images/c01-i0222.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> and their corresponding eigenvectors ![bold-italic h 1 comma ellipsis comma bold-italic h Subscript p Baseline](images/c01-i0223.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math>. As above, define the matrix ![bold-italic upper H equals left-parenthesis bold-italic h 1 comma ellipsis comma bold-italic h Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis comma bold-italic upper D equals diag left-parenthesis lamda 1 comma ellipsis comma lamda Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0224.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">h</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext>diag</mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> and ![bold-italic upper D Superscript 1 slash 2 Baseline colon equals diag left-parenthesis StartRoot lamda 1 EndRoot comma ellipsis comma StartRoot lamda Subscript p Baseline EndRoot right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0225.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mtext>diag</mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></msqrt><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>. Recall that ![bold-italic upper A equals bold-italic upper H bold-italic upper D bold-italic upper H Superscript down-tack](images/c01-i0226.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup></math>. The *symmetric square root* of ![bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0227.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math> is given by ![bold-italic upper A Superscript 1 slash 2 Baseline colon equals bold-italic upper H bold-italic upper D Superscript 1 slash 2 Baseline bold-italic upper H Superscript down-tack](images/c01-i0228.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup></math>; indeed, a simple calculation gives ![bold-italic upper A Superscript 1 slash 2 Baseline bold-italic upper A Superscript 1 slash 2 Baseline equals bold-italic upper H bold-italic upper D Superscript 1 slash 2 Baseline bold-italic upper H Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic upper H bold-italic upper D Superscript 1 slash 2 Baseline bold-italic upper H Superscript down-tack Baseline equals bold-italic upper H bold-italic upper D bold-italic upper H Superscript down-tack Baseline equals bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0229.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">D</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">H</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></math>.

All the above matrix concepts can be implemented in both **R** and Python by using built-in matrix functions. Let us continue with the blue chips dataset in [Example 1.1](#c01.xhtml#c01-fea-0006). The Python code `S_2002.T` returns the transpose of ![bold-italic upper S](images/c01-i0230.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">S</mi></mrow></math> from the 2002 dataset, `@` computes matrix multiplication, and so on. All the codings for other related computations can be found in [Programme 1.3](#c01.xhtml#c01-gra-0003) for Python (resp. [Programme 1.4](#c01.xhtml#c01-gra-0004) for **R**).

![](images/c01-gra-0004.png)![](images/c01-gra-0005.png)![](images/c01-gra-0006.png)

**(VII) Algorithm for Cholesky Decomposition**

The *Cholesky decomposition* of a ![p times p](images/c01-i0231.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></math> positive definite matrix ![bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0232.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math> is to find a ![p times p](images/c01-i0233.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></math> upper triangular matrix ![bold-italic upper C](images/c01-i0234.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math> such that ![bold-italic upper C Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic upper C equals bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0235.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></math>. Let ![bold-italic upper A equals left-parenthesis a Subscript i j Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0236.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> and ![bold-italic upper C equals left-parenthesis c Subscript i j Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0237.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> where ![c Subscript i j Baseline equals 0](images/c01-i0238.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> whenever ![i greater-than j](images/c01-i0239.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>i</mi><mo>&#62;</mo><mi>j</mi></math>. The following steps describe how to find ![bold-italic upper C](images/c01-i0240.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math> from a given matrix ![bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0241.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math>:

1.  *Step 1*. Set ![c 11 equals StartRoot a 11 EndRoot](images/c01-i0242.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>11</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mrow></msqrt></math>, and ![c Subscript 1 j Baseline equals a Subscript 1 j Baseline slash c 11](images/c01-i0243.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></math> for ![j equals 2 comma ellipsis comma p](images/c01-i0244.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></math>.
2.  *Step 2*. For ![i equals 2 comma ellipsis comma p](images/c01-i0245.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></math>, set ![c Subscript i i Baseline equals StartRoot a Subscript i i Baseline minus sigma-summation Underscript k equals 1 Overscript i minus 1 Endscripts c Subscript k i Superscript 2 Baseline EndRoot comma and c Subscript i j Baseline equals StartFraction 1 Over c Subscript i i Baseline EndFraction left-parenthesis a Subscript i j Baseline minus sigma-summation Underscript k equals 1 Overscript i minus 1 Endscripts c Subscript k i Baseline c Subscript k j Baseline right-parenthesis comma for j equals i plus 1 comma ellipsis comma p period](images/c01-math-0025.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><munderover><mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></msqrt><mtext>, and</mtext><mspace width="0.15em"/><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><munderover><mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced><mtext>, for</mtext><mspace width="0.15em"/><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mtext>.</mtext></math> 

To see why this algorithm can give a valid ![bold-italic upper C](images/c01-i0246.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math>, note that the ![left-parenthesis i comma j right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0247.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> element of ![bold-italic upper C Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic upper C equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 1 Overscript p Endscripts c Subscript k i Baseline c Subscript k j Baseline equals a Subscript i j](images/c01-i0248.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8721;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math>. When ![i equals 1](images/c01-i0249.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and ![j equals 1](images/c01-i0250.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, ![c 11 squared equals a 11](images/c01-i0251.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msubsup><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></math>, and so we simply take ![c 11 equals StartRoot a 11 EndRoot](images/c01-i0252.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>11</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mrow></msqrt></math>. When ![i equals 1](images/c01-i0253.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and ![j equals 2 comma ellipsis comma p](images/c01-i0254.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></math>, ![a Subscript 1 j Baseline equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 1 Overscript p Endscripts c Subscript k Baseline 1 Baseline c Subscript k j Baseline equals c 11 c Subscript 1 j](images/c01-i0255.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8721;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>11</mn></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></math> since ![c Subscript k Baseline 1 Baseline equals 0](images/c01-i0256.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> for ![k equals 2 comma ellipsis comma p](images/c01-i0257.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></math>, therefore ![c Subscript 1 j Baseline equals a Subscript 1 j Baseline slash c 11](images/c01-i0258.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></math>. For ![i equals 2 comma ellipsis comma p](images/c01-i0259.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></math>, ![a Subscript i i Baseline equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 1 Overscript p Endscripts c Subscript k i Superscript 2 Baseline equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 1 Overscript i Endscripts c Subscript k i Superscript 2 Baseline equals sigma-summation Underscript k equals 1 Overscript i minus 1 Endscripts c Subscript k i Superscript 2 Baseline plus c Subscript i i Superscript 2](images/c01-i0260.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8721;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><msubsup><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8721;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></msubsup><msubsup><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8721;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><msubsup><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></math> since ![c Subscript i j Baseline equals 0](images/c01-i0261.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> for ![i greater-than j](images/c01-i0262.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>i</mi><mo>&#62;</mo><mi>j</mi></math>, we then take

![c Subscript i i Baseline equals StartRoot a Subscript i i Baseline minus sigma-summation Underscript k equals 1 Overscript i minus 1 Endscripts c Subscript k i Superscript 2 Baseline EndRoot period](images/c01-math-0026.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><munderover><mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></msqrt><mo>.</mo></math> 

Finally, for ![j equals i plus 1 comma ellipsis comma p](images/c01-i0263.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></math>,

1 Over c Subscript i i Baseline EndFraction left-parenthesis a Subscript i j Baseline minus sigma-summation Underscript k equals 1 Overscript i minus 1 Endscripts c Subscript k i Baseline c Subscript stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8658;</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mfenced  

## 1.3 VECTORS AND MATRIX NORMS

The notion of a norm is to measure the length of different abstract objects. Here we recall some useful results and commonly used norms for vectors and matrices.

**(I) Vector norm**

We consider the space ![double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0264.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math>, such that each ![bold-italic x element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0265.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math> is a ![p](images/c01-i0266.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>\-dimensional vector. A function ![phi colon double-struck upper R Superscript p Baseline right-arrow double-struck upper R](images/c01-i0267.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>&#8594;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi></math> is a **norm** for the Euclidean space ![double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0268.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math> if it satisfies:

1.  positivity: ![phi left-parenthesis bold-italic x right-parenthesis greater-than-or-equal-to 0](images/c01-i0269.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8805;</mo><mn>0</mn></math> for all ![bold-italic x element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0270.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math>, and ![phi left-parenthesis bold-italic x right-parenthesis equals 0 left right double arrow bold-italic x equals bold 0](images/c01-i0271.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mspace width="2.77695pt"/><mo>&#x021D4;</mo><mspace width="2.77695pt"/><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></math>;
2.  triangle inequality: for any ![bold-italic x comma bold-italic y element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0272.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math>, ![phi left-parenthesis bold-italic x plus bold-italic y right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to phi left-parenthesis bold-italic x right-parenthesis plus phi left-parenthesis bold-italic y right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0273.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>;
3.  absolute homogeneity: for any ![bold-italic x element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0274.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math> and scalar ![a element-of double-struck upper R](images/c01-i0275.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi></math>, ![phi left-parenthesis a bold-italic x right-parenthesis equals StartAbsoluteValue a EndAbsoluteValue phi left-parenthesis bold-italic x right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0276.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>.

One of the most commonly encountered norms is the ![q](images/c01-i0277.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norm: for ![bold-italic x equals left-parenthesis x 1 comma ellipsis comma x Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript down-tack Baseline element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0278.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math> and ![q greater-than-or-equal-to 1](images/c01-i0279.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8805;</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, the ![q](images/c01-i0280.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norm is defined by:

![double-vertical-bar bold-italic x double-vertical-bar Subscript q Baseline colon equals left-parenthesis sigma-summation Underscript i equals 1 Overscript p Endscripts StartAbsoluteValue x Subscript i Baseline EndAbsoluteValue Superscript q Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript StartFraction 1 Over q EndFraction Baseline period](images/c01-math-0028.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><mrow><munderover><mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>p</mi></munderover><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>q</mi></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> 

The case when ![q equals infinity](images/c01-i0281.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>&#8734;</mi></math> is defined in a different way; indeed, the ![infinity](images/c01-i0282.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#8734;</mi></mrow></math>\-norm, properly called sup-norm, is defined as

![double-vertical-bar bold-italic x double-vertical-bar Subscript infinity Baseline colon equals max Underscript 1 less-than-or-equal-to i less-than-or-equal-to p Endscripts StartAbsoluteValue x Subscript i Baseline EndAbsoluteValue period](images/c01-math-0029.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi>&#8734;</mi></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><munder><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></munder><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mo>.</mo></math> 

When ![q equals 0](images/c01-i0283.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, we define the “0-norm” by the number of non-zero entries in ![x](images/c01-i0284.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>. The 0-norm is not a norm as it fails to satisfy the homogeneity condition.

**(II) Matrix norm**

The concept of a norm can be extended to the space ![double-struck upper R Superscript p times k](images/c01-i0285.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></math> of ![p times k](images/c01-i0286.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>k</mi></math> matrices. A function ![phi colon double-struck upper R Superscript p times k Baseline right-arrow double-struck upper R](images/c01-i0287.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo>:</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo>&#8594;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi></math> is a **norm** for the space ![double-struck upper R Superscript p times k](images/c01-i0288.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></math> if it satisfies

1.  positivity: ![phi left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis greater-than-or-equal-to 0](images/c01-i0289.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8805;</mo><mn>0</mn></math> for all ![bold-italic upper A element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p times k](images/c01-i0290.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></math>, and ![phi left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis equals 0 left right double arrow bold-italic upper A equals bold 0](images/c01-i0291.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mspace width="2.77695pt"/><mo>&#x021D4;</mo><mspace width="2.77695pt"/><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></math>;
2.  triangle inequality: for any ![bold-italic upper A comma bold-italic upper B element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p times k](images/c01-i0292.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">B</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></math>, ![phi left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A plus bold-italic upper B right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to phi left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis plus phi left-parenthesis bold-italic upper B right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0293.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>;
3.  homogeneity: for any ![bold-italic upper A element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p times k](images/c01-i0294.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></math> and scalar ![a element-of double-struck upper R](images/c01-i0295.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>a</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi></math>, ![phi left-parenthesis a bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis equals StartAbsoluteValue a EndAbsoluteValue phi left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0296.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>.

In addition, if ![p equals k](images/c01-i0297.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></math> and ![phi](images/c01-i0298.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi></mrow></math> satisfies

1.  sub-multiplicativity: ![phi left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A bold-italic upper B right-parenthesis less-than-or-equal-to phi left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis phi left-parenthesis bold-italic upper B right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0299.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> for any ![bold-italic upper A element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p times k](images/c01-i0300.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></math>,

then ![phi](images/c01-i0301.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi></mrow></math> is said to be a **sub-multiplicative norm**.

There are several common examples of matrix norms. In particular, the ![q](images/c01-i0302.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norm for square matrices is commonly used. A matrix norm ![parallel-to dot parallel-to](images/c01-i0303.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo><mo>&#183;</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo></math> on ![double-struck upper R Superscript p times p](images/c01-i0304.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></math> is said to be *compatible* with a vector norm ![parallel-to dot parallel-to Subscript v Baseline](images/c01-i0305.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo><mo>&#183;</mo><mspace width="0.3em"/><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo><mi>v</mi></msub></math> on ![double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0306.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math> if for any ![bold-italic upper A element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p times p](images/c01-i0307.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></math> and ![bold-italic x element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0308.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math>, it holds that

![double-vertical-bar bold-italic upper A bold-italic x double-vertical-bar Subscript v Baseline less-than-or-equal-to double-vertical-bar bold-italic upper A double-vertical-bar dot double-vertical-bar bold-italic x double-vertical-bar Subscript v Baseline period](images/c01-math-0030.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>&#8804;</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mo>&#183;</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>.</mo></math> 

Let ![parallel-to dot parallel-to Subscript q Baseline](images/c01-i0309.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo><mo>&#183;</mo><mspace width="0.3em"/><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo><mi>q</mi></msub></math> be the vector ![q](images/c01-i0310.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norm on ![double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0311.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math>. Then the ![q](images/c01-i0312.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norm ![parallel-to dot parallel-to](images/c01-i0313.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo><mo>&#183;</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo></math> on the space of ![p times p](images/c01-i0314.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></math> square matrices is defined as

[(1.3)](#c01.xhtml#R_c01-disp-0030)![double-vertical-bar bold-italic upper A double-vertical-bar equals max Underscript bold-italic x not-equals bold 0 Endscripts StartFraction double-vertical-bar bold-italic upper A bold-italic x double-vertical-bar Subscript q Baseline Over double-vertical-bar bold-italic x double-vertical-bar Subscript q Baseline EndFraction equals max Underscript parallel-to bold-italic x parallel-to equals 1 Endscripts double-vertical-bar bold-italic upper A bold-italic x double-vertical-bar Subscript q Baseline comma bold-italic upper A element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p times p Baseline period](images/c01-math-0031.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mo>=</mo><munder><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8800;</mo><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><munder><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mspace width="1em"/><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> 

It is clear that this definition verifies the properties of a matrix norm. In addition, it is obvious that the ![q](images/c01-i0315.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norms for square matrices and vectors are compatible. The definition can easily be generalized to ![p times k](images/c01-i0316.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>k</mi></math> matrices, by considering the norm ![double-vertical-bar bold-italic upper A bold-italic x double-vertical-bar Subscript q](images/c01-i0317.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi>q</mi></msub></math> in ([1.3](#c01.xhtml#c01-disp-0030)) as the ![q](images/c01-i0318.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norm of ![bold-italic upper A bold-italic x](images/c01-i0319.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></math> in ![double-struck upper R Superscript p](images/c01-i0320.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></math> for any ![bold-italic x element-of double-struck upper R Superscript k](images/c01-i0321.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></math> which possesses the corresponding ![q](images/c01-i0322.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norm in ![double-struck upper R Superscript k](images/c01-i0323.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></math>. In the following, without the risk of causing any ambiguity, we shall denote the ![q](images/c01-i0324.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norms for both vectors and matrices by ![parallel-to dot parallel-to Subscript q Baseline](images/c01-i0325.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo><mo>&#183;</mo><mspace width="0.3em"/><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8741;</mo><mi>q</mi></msub></math>. Below are several important special cases of the ![q](images/c01-i0326.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norm for ![p times k](images/c01-i0327.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>k</mi></math> matrices:

1.  1-norm: ![double-vertical-bar bold-italic upper A double-vertical-bar Subscript 1 Baseline equals max Underscript j equals 1 comma ellipsis comma k Endscripts left-parenthesis sigma-summation Underscript i equals 1 Overscript p Endscripts StartAbsoluteValue a Subscript i j Baseline EndAbsoluteValue right-parenthesis period](images/c01-math-0032.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><munder><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mspace width="0.125em"/><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></munder><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><mrow><munderover><mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>p</mi></munderover><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> 
2.  2-norm (a.k.a. the *spectral norm*): ![double-vertical-bar bold-italic upper A double-vertical-bar Subscript 2 Baseline equals StartRoot lamda Subscript max Baseline left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis EndRoot comma](images/c01-math-0033.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msqrt><mo>,</mo></math> where ![lamda Subscript max Baseline left-parenthesis bold-italic upper A Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic upper A right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0328.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> is the maximum eigenvalue of the matrix ![bold-italic upper A Superscript down-tack Baseline bold-italic upper A](images/c01-i0329.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></math>.
3.  ![infinity](images/c01-i0330.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#8734;</mi></mrow></math>\-norm/sup-norm: ![double-vertical-bar bold-italic upper A double-vertical-bar Subscript infinity Baseline equals max Underscript i equals 1 comma ellipsis comma p Endscripts left-parenthesis sigma-summation Underscript j equals 1 Overscript k Endscripts StartAbsoluteValue a Subscript i j Baseline EndAbsoluteValue right-parenthesis period](images/c01-math-0034.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi><msub><mo stretchy="false">&#8214;</mo><mi>&#8734;</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><munder><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mspace width="0.125em"/><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></munder><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><mrow><munderover><mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></munderover><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> 

Apart from the ![q](images/c01-i0331.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>\-norm, another commonly encountered matrix norm in machine learning and deep learning is the *Frobenius norm*, which is defined as

## 1.4 COMMON PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS

In this section, we shall review some basic probability distributions learnt in elementary statistical courses. Readers may refer to [\[10](#c01.xhtml#c01-bib-0010), [13\]](#c01.xhtml#c01-bib-0013) for more a comprehensive treatment of this topic, and [\[1](#c01.xhtml#c01-bib-0001), [14](#c01.xhtml#c01-bib-0014), [17\]](#c01.xhtml#c01-bib-0017) for a more advanced discussion, and on tackling block matrices in particular. These distributions are important and serve as the building blocks for constructing and deriving the null distributions of many test statistics. Throughout the book, “iid” stands for “*independent and identically distributed*”, referring to an underlying family of random variables.

 

### 1.4.1 Univariate Distributions

To begin with, we review the definitions and related important properties of several commonly used univariate distributions.

1.  **Normal distribution:** ![script upper N left-parenthesis mu comma sigma squared right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0332.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#956;</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>. A real random variable ![normal x](images/c01-i0333.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mrow></math> is said to follow a normal distribution with a mean ![mu](images/c01-i0334.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#956;</mi></mrow></math> and variance ![sigma squared](images/c01-i0335.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, denoted as ![normal x tilde script upper N left-parenthesis mu comma sigma squared right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0336.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>&#8764;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#956;</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, if its *probability density function* (pdf) takes the form: (1.4)![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals StartFraction 1 Over StartRoot 2 pi sigma squared EndRoot EndFraction exp left-brace minus StartFraction left-parenthesis x minus mu right-parenthesis squared Over 2 sigma squared EndFraction right-brace comma x element-of double-struck upper R period](images/c01-math-0036.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>&#960;</mi><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mfenced open="{" close="}" separators=""><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>&#956;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mspace width="1em"/><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mo>.</mo></math> 
2.  **Chi-square distribution:** ![chi Subscript nu Superscript 2](images/c01-i0337.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msubsup><mrow><mi>&#967;</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>&#957;</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></math>. A non-negative random variable ![normal x](images/c01-i0338.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mrow></math> is said to follow a chi-square distribution with degrees of freedom ![nu element-of double-struck upper N](images/c01-i0339.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>&#957;</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">N</mi></math>, denoted by ![normal x tilde chi Subscript nu Superscript 2](images/c01-i0340.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>&#8764;</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi>&#967;</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>&#957;</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></math>, if its pdf takes the form:
    
    (1.5)![f left-parenthesis x right-parenthesis equals StartFraction 1 Over 2 Superscript nu slash 2 Baseline normal upper Gamma left-parenthesis nu slash 2 right-parenthesis EndFraction x Superscript nu slash 2 minus 1 Baseline e Superscript negative x slash 2 Baseline comma x greater-than 0 comma](images/c01-math-0037.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>&#957;</mi><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">&#915;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#957;</mi><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>&#957;</mi><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mspace width="1em"/><mi>x</mi><mo>&#62;</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></math> 
    
    where ![normal upper Gamma left-parenthesis dot right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0341.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="normal">&#915;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>&#183;</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> is the well-known gamma function:

    If ![normal z 1 comma ellipsis comma normal z Subscript n Baseline](images/c01-i0342.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">z</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></math> are iid ![script upper N left-parenthesis 0 comma 1 right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0343.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> random variables, then one can easily show that ![normal x equals normal z 1 squared plus midline-horizontal-ellipsis plus normal z Subscript n Superscript 2 Baseline tilde chi Subscript n Superscript 2](images/c01-i0344.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mi>&#8943;</mi><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">z</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>&#8764;</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi>&#967;</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></math>. Furthermore, if ![normal y 1 comma ellipsis comma normal y Subscript n Baseline](images/c01-i0345.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></math> are iid ![script upper N left-parenthesis mu comma sigma squared right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0346.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#956;</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, we also have the following distribution of the sample variance ![normal s Subscript normal y Superscript 2](images/c01-i0347.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></math>:

    this result is just a special case of [Proposition 1.2](#c01.xhtml#c01-fea-0008), which we will meet shortly.



### 1.4.2 The Multivariate Normal Distribution

The random vector ![bold x equals left-parenthesis normal x 1 comma ellipsis comma normal x Subscript p Baseline right-parenthesis Superscript down-tack](images/c01-i0386.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup></math> is said to follow a ![p](images/c01-i0387.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>\-variate normal distribution with a mean vector ![bold-italic mu](images/c01-i0388.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi></mrow></math> and covariance matrix ![bold upper Sigma](images/c01-i0389.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi></mrow></math>,

(1.6)![f left-parenthesis bold-italic x right-parenthesis equals StartFraction 1 Over left-parenthesis 2 pi right-parenthesis Superscript p slash 2 Baseline StartAbsoluteValue bold upper Sigma EndAbsoluteValue Superscript 1 slash 2 Baseline EndFraction exp left-brace minus one half left-parenthesis bold-italic x minus bold-italic mu right-parenthesis Superscript down-tack Baseline bold upper Sigma Superscript negative 1 Baseline left-parenthesis bold-italic x minus bold-italic mu right-parenthesis right-brace comma bold-italic x element-of double-struck upper R Superscript p Baseline period](images/c01-math-0043.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>&#960;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mfenced open="{" close="}" separators=""><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mspace width="1em"/><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>.</mo></math> 

The following are some important properties of the multivariate normal distribution:

1.  Consider ![bold x tilde script upper N Subscript p Baseline left-parenthesis bold-italic mu comma bold upper Sigma right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0392.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mo>&#8764;</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, then for a deterministic ![bold-italic upper B element-of double-struck upper R Superscript q times p](images/c01-i0393.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">B</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></math> and ![bold-italic b element-of double-struck upper R Superscript q](images/c01-i0394.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></math>, we have ![bold y equals bold-italic upper B bold x plus bold-italic b tilde script upper N Subscript q Baseline left-parenthesis bold-italic upper B bold-italic mu plus bold-italic b comma bold-italic upper B bold upper Sigma bold-italic upper B Superscript down-tack Baseline right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0395.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold">y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">B</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mi><mo>&#8764;</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi></mrow><mi>q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">B</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">B</mi><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">B</mi><mo>&#8868;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>.
2.  Let ![bold x 1 comma ellipsis comma bold x Subscript n Baseline tilde Overscript iid Endscripts script upper N Subscript p Baseline left-parenthesis bold-italic mu comma bold upper Sigma right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0396.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mover class="overset"><mo>&#8764;</mo><mtext>iid</mtext></mover><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>. Let ![bold x 1 comma ellipsis comma bold x Subscript n Baseline](images/c01-i0403.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></math> be ![p](images/c01-i0404.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>\-dimensional iid random vectors from an arbitrary distribution with a finite mean ![bold-italic mu](images/c01-i0405.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi></mrow></math> and finite covariance matrix ![bold upper Sigma](images/c01-i0406.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi></mrow></math>. Then ![StartRoot n EndRoot left-parenthesis bold x overbar minus bold-italic mu right-parenthesis tilde script upper N Subscript p Baseline left-parenthesis bold 0 comma bold upper Sigma right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0407.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msqrt><mi>n</mi></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8764;</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> approximately for a large enough sample size ![n](images/c01-i0408.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> (relative to ![p](images/c01-i0409.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>).

This is a direct consequence of an application of *Slutsky's theorem* by replacing ![bold-italic mu](images/c01-i0418.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi></mrow></math> by ![bold-italic x overbar](images/c01-i0419.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover></math> and ![bold upper Sigma](images/c01-i0420.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi></mrow></math> by ![bold-italic upper S](images/c01-i0421.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">S</mi></mrow></math> in Property 4 above.

In simple linear regression, we often use the marginal and conditional distributions of the bivariate normal distribution; the corresponding results are readily extended to the multivariate case for their application in the context of multiple linear regression.

### 1.4.3 Wishart Distribution

The *Wishart distribution* is a multivariate extension of the chi-square distribution. Recall Property 2 of [Subsection 1.4.1](#c01.xhtml#c01-sec-0010), namely if ![normal x 1 comma ellipsis comma normal x Subscript n Baseline](images/c01-i0462.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></math> are iid distributed as ![script upper N left-parenthesis mu comma sigma squared right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0463.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#956;</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, then

![sigma-summation Underscript i equals 1 Overscript n Endscripts StartFraction left-parenthesis normal x Subscript i Baseline minus normal x overbar right-parenthesis squared Over sigma squared EndFraction equals StartFraction left-parenthesis n minus 1 right-parenthesis normal s squared Over sigma squared EndFraction tilde chi Subscript n minus 1 Superscript 2 Baseline period](images/c01-math-0046.png)<math display="block" overflow="scroll"><munderover><mrow><mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></munderover><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>&#8764;</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi>&#967;</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>.</mo></math>

By virtue of ([1.9](#c01.xhtml#c01-disp-0051)) and the very definition of the Wishart distribution, we can then see that ![bold upper A tilde upper W Subscript p Baseline left-parenthesis bold upper Sigma comma n minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0502.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi><mo>&#8764;</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, and therefore ![bold upper S tilde upper W Subscript p Baseline left-parenthesis StartFraction 1 Over n minus 1 EndFraction bold upper Sigma comma n minus 1 right-parenthesis](images/c01-i0503.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi mathvariant="bold">S</mi><mo>&#8764;</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mi mathvariant="bold">&#931;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>. The independence of ![bold upper S](images/c01-i0504.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">S</mi></mrow></math> and ![bold x overbar](images/c01-i0505.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover></math> is inherited from the independence of ![bold upper A](images/c01-i0506.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi></mrow></math> and ![bold z Subscript n](images/c01-i0507.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">z</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></math>, also due to ([1.9](#c01.xhtml#c01-disp-0051)).

 

## 1.5 INTRODUCTORY BAYESIAN STATISTICS

A Bayesian approach to the estimation of parameters is a probabilistic method in which an optimal decision rule is taken, in contrast to the usual maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) method. Compared with MLE, whose resulting ![ModifyingAbove theta With Ì‚](images/c01-i0511.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#952;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></math> maximizes the probability of obtaining the given sample of training dataset, the Bayesian approach evaluates the conditional probability of ![normal theta](images/c01-i0512.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#952;</mi></mrow></math> given the sample taking various values instead; see [Figure 1.1](#c01.xhtml#c01-fig-0001) for an illustration of the comparison. Indeed, for *Bayesian inference*, the training stage updates our prior belief on the probabilities of ![normal theta](images/c01-i0513.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#952;</mi></mrow></math> using the input data, resulting in posterior probabilities as shown in [Figure 1.1](#c01.xhtml#c01-fig-0001)b.

The theoretical foundation of Bayesian inference is based on an extended form of *Bayes' theorem*: Let ![upper A 1 comma ellipsis comma upper A Subscript n Baseline](images/c01-i0514.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8230;</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></math> be mutually exclusive events and ![union upper A Subscript i Baseline equals colon upper A](images/c01-i0515.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><msubsup><mrow><mo>&#8746;</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>:</mo><mi>A</mi></math>. Then, for any event ![upper B subset-of-or-equal-to upper A](images/c01-i0516.png)<math display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mi>B</mi><mo>&#8838;</mo><mi>A</mi></math>, we have
